Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with shortness of breath.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Patient: Yeah. I was watching TV and, um, just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Shortness of breath began about one hour ago.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Yeah. I was watching TV and, um, just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Shortness of breath started while sitting and watching TV.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: That is, while you're sitting watching TV? Patient: Yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No prior episodes of similar shortness of breath.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: And, have you noticed anything like this before? Patient: Um, no.
Patient: Um, so, I , I started with a cough yesterday.
Doctor: So, talk to me about the cough. Have you bought anything up? Patient: Uh, no, I haven't, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not think the shortness of breath is worsening.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: And, this shortness of breath you're having, is it getting worse? Patient: Um. Patient: No. I mean, I don't know.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports a sensation of heart racing/palpitations.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: No. I mean, I don't know. I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart, it's really going.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Denies chest pain associated with the shortness of breath.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: And, the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest? Patient: Um, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Chest feels sore with deep inspiration.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: How about when you take a very deep breath in? Patient: Um, I mean, yeah. My chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar. You know, it's, it's all tender.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Last respiratory illness was a few months ago.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doctor: And, when was the last time you were ill with the flu, or symptoms like this? Patient: Um, you know, I get coughs and colds quite a lot, but probably. Patient: Good few months ago.

Past_Medical_History.content: Cesarean section performed four weeks ago.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Patient: Yeah. I, I don't know if it's, um, relevant, but I had a C-section a few weeks ago. Doctor: OK. And, how long ago was that? Just a few weeks? Patient: Yeah, four weeks.
Doctor: And, apart from the C-section and the shortness of breath, have you got any other medical problems I should know about? Patient: Um, no.

Medications.source_text: Patient: Uh, they gave me some, uh, Codeine.

Medications.content: Patient had been taking codeine fairly regularly after the C-section.
Medications.source_text: Patient: Uh, yeah. I, I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly.

Medications.content: Patient has not taken codeine for about one week.
Medications.source_text: Patient: But, probably haven't taken it for a week.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Patient: tell you, I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.

Family_History.content: Mother has a history of leg blood clots.
Family_History.source_text: Patient: OK. Yeah. I mean, my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is currently with her baby.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Doctor: And, are you with baby at the moment? Patient: Yes, I am.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Baby has no coughs or colds.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Doctor: OK. Any coughs or colds with, uh, them? Patient: No, no. He's fine.

Social_and_Family_History.content: No one else is at home; partner is at work.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Doctor: Is anyone else with you at home? Patient: Uh, no. My partner's at work.

Assessment.content: Concern for possible blood clots (deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism) given recent C-section and acute shortness of breath.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: So, what I'm worried about at the moment is, given that you've had a C-section Doctor: Some people can suffer with clots. And, those can either be found in the legs or your chest, so in your lungs.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to go to the hospital for further evaluation now.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: It might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out the bit further. Doctor: So, I think that's the best thing to do, for the time being.

Plan_of_Care.content: Offered ambulance transport or self-transport to the hospital.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: So, there's two ways of us doing this. The first is, I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient chose to self-transport to the hospital with her baby.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Patient: Uh, it feels a bit dramatic to call an ambulance. Um, I, I will, I will go. I will, I will take myself.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to go fairly quickly and take supplies for the baby.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Sure. And, what I would suggest is, go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised not to take codeine for the time being.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And, if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being.

Plan_of_Care.content: Informed that if a clot is found, treatment to reduce the clot can be given at the hospital.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And, if it, if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot.

Physical_Findings.content: Heart rate is slightly fast on self-measured pulse.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Doctor: So, your heart is running slightly fast at the moment, which is probably because of the shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under.
